answer: Agents can escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake before joining a market, then earn access to valuable tasks only after completing work that peers validate. If an agent is caught fabricating identities or colluding, the protocol slashes its stake and rejects linked claims. Spawning a hundred Sybils therefore requires funding a hundred escrows, while one real account can reuse its reputation. The dune, glacier, and pigment labels might classify task domains, but they do not replace the costly stake that makes fake identities expensive.
